manifest.scope: complete recursive file set under sources/original and sources/converted

records.claim_text: MEASNET requires at least 12 complete consecutive months of measurement for at least one mast at the site.
records.title: Evaluation of Site-Specific Wind Conditions
records.paraphrased_support: The procedure specifies a 12-month complete and consecutive measurement period for at least one site mast so seasonal variation is represented.
records.limitations: The earlier 2022 URL recorded by the ingress evaluation returned 404 on 2026-08-12; this is the current official publisher path. The PDF identifies itself as Version 3, not Version 3.1.

records.claim_text: MEASNET treats incomplete measurement as a deviation that must be disclosed and included in uncertainty.
records.title: Evaluation of Site-Specific Wind Conditions
records.paraphrased_support: The procedure requires deviations to be identified, summarized, assessed for significance, and reflected as uncertainty; measurement below the specified completeness criteria is expressly a deviation.
records.limitations: This does not establish that a lender must waive the deviation or that disclosure alone makes a zero-measurement assessment bankable.

records.claim_text: The MEASNET site-assessment procedure is based on site-specific and on-site measurements.
records.title: Evaluation of Site-Specific Wind Conditions
records.paraphrased_support: MEASNET describes gathering on-site measurement as the first phase and identifies site-specific measurements as the assessment basis.
records.limitations: The procedure is broader than energy-yield bankability and does not itself state DutchBay financing conditions.

records.claim_text: IEC 61400-15-1:2025 defines a framework covering measurement, prediction, assessment reporting, and traceability.
records.title: IEC 61400-15-1:2025 - Site suitability input conditions for wind power plants
records.paraphrased_support: The official scope covers definition, measurement, and prediction of long-term site characteristics and traceable reporting.
records.limitations: Only the official public scope was available; the full 80-page standard is paywalled. The public scope does not state a 12-month mast requirement, so that rule is attributed to MEASNET unless a licensed IEC clause is obtained.

records.claim_text: A measurement campaign is a transaction condition precedent rather than a disclosure question.
records.title: Evaluation of Site-Specific Wind Conditions
records.paraphrased_support: MEASNET establishes a site-measurement procedure and deviation/uncertainty treatment. It does not establish an unwaivable DutchBay financing condition precedent.
records.limitations: The standard does not prescribe DutchBay loan conditions, make a deviation legally unwaivable, or call measurement a financing condition precedent. Facility terms, lender credit approval and independent-engineer requirements remain unavailable transaction evidence.

records.claim_text: An ADB document contains 1.35x and 1.50x debt-service-related thresholds.
records.title: Indonesia Java-Bali 500-Kilovolt Power Transmission Crossing Project Completion Report
records.paraphrased_support: The project agreement required PLN net revenues of 1.35 times and later 1.50 times estimated maximum debt service before incurring debt; the completion report also records noncompliance and waiver/acceptance history.
records.limitations: This is a sovereign utility corporate debt-incurrence covenant, not a universal project-finance policy, not an IFC rule, and not a common threshold for DSCR, LLCR, and PLCR.

records.claim_text: A World Bank-supported power project reported a 1.35x minimum base-case DSCR and approximately 1.51x average DSCR.
records.title: Vietnam Phu My 2 Phase 2 Power Project - Project Appraisal Document
records.paraphrased_support: The project's base case shows a 1.35 minimum annual DSCR and 1.51 average annual DSCR.
records.limitations: This is one 2002 Vietnam gas-power transaction with an IDA partial risk guarantee; it is precedent, not a current universal DFI policy or a DutchBay-specific requirement.

records.claim_text: Official World Bank analysis describes a likely 1.25x-1.35x minimum DSCR for a modeled project-financing case.
records.title: El Desarrollo Hidroelectrico en el Peru
records.paraphrased_support: The analysis says its typical project-financing case would probably require a minimum DSCR in the 1.25-1.35 range; a blended IFI/commercial case produces 1.40.
records.limitations: This is a modeled Peruvian hydropower sector example, not a binding lender policy and not directly comparable to DutchBay's currency, offtaker, resource, and debt risks.

records.claim_text: There is a universal IFC/ADB 1.35x-1.50x minimum band applicable equally to DSCR, LLCR, and PLCR for DutchBay.
records.title: Official project and sector financing examples
records.paraphrased_support: The official examples are context-specific, use different ratio definitions and borrower structures, and span at least 1.25 to 1.50.
records.limitations: No directly relevant IFC or ADB policy, DutchBay term sheet, credit approval, or financing document has been produced. A DutchBay covenant recommendation may still be professionally defensible, but must be labeled analyst judgment and separately defined for each ratio.

artifact_exception.reason: This row is an explicit claim-boundary inference over the six hashed official records in supporting_record_ids; it has no separate publisher original and must not be presented as primary source text.

records.claim_text: The architecture map contains 72 unique RS identifiers, not 70.
records.title: Architecture and Dependency Map
records.paraphrased_support: The six families contain 15, 9, 12, 12, 13, and 11 identifiers, totaling 72.
records.limitations: Pointer status and investigated coverage must be recalculated from the controlled 72-item register; identifier presence is not confirmation of the underlying risk claim.

records.claim_text: The audited tree contains 29 top-level YAML artefacts, not 29 total scenario artefacts.
records.title: Git tree under scenarios/
records.paraphrased_support: The audited tree has 29 top-level YAML, 5 top-level JSON, and 39 YAML/JSON artefacts including nested paths.
records.limitations: Artefact count does not imply every file is a runnable production scenario; the set includes examples, tests, overrides, scratch/bad fixtures, and frozen AEP summaries.

records.claim_text: No executed or indicative lender term sheet had been produced to substantiate a DutchBay-specific DSRA covenant; six months remains an assumption pending lender communication.
records.title: Issue #920: confirm 6-month DSRA target against the CEB-PPA lender term sheet
records.paraphrased_support: The open control issue records a prior repository/Downloads search, finds no executed or indicative term sheet, and retains six months only as an unconfirmed market assumption.
records.limitations: This is an internal evidence-status record, not a lender document and not proof that no off-repository communication exists. The issue is mutable after the archived snapshot and remains open.

records.claim_text: A 2025 World Bank/IDA Sri Lanka programme document describes legacy CEB PPA payment-security structures sized to cover 12 months of PPA payments.
records.title: Secure, Affordable, and Sustainable Energy for Sri Lanka - Project Appraisal Document
records.paraphrased_support: The PAD explains that existing payment-security sizing under the respective PPAs covers 12 months of payments and is costly because CEB must provide cash collateral for the issuing banks.
records.limitations: This is offtaker/PPA payment security, not a debt-service reserve account. It describes a programme context and does not establish DutchBay's executed contractual terms.

records.claim_text: The same 2025 programme expects IDA-backed standby letters of credit to cover six to nine months of CEB payment obligations under relevant PPAs.
records.title: Secure, Affordable, and Sustainable Energy for Sri Lanka - Project Appraisal Document
records.paraphrased_support: The proposed IDA guarantee would backstop CEB's PPA payment obligations through an international-bank SBLC expected to cover six to nine months of payments for the underlying debt tenor.
records.limitations: This is a proposed programme payment-security mechanism, not DSRA sizing and not evidence that DutchBay has obtained the guarantee. The PAD describes expected terms rather than an executed DutchBay instrument.

records.claim_text: A final published IEC 61400-15-2 standard supports the audit's IEC-default and IEC-convention claims.
records.title: IEC Webstore catalogue search for 61400-15-2
records.page_or_section: official catalogue API; valid and all-state searches
records.paraphrased_support: The official public catalogue returned zero primary, secondary, and tertiary results for 61400-15-2 with both validOnly true and false; a positive-control query returned IEC 61400-15-1:2025.
records.limitations: This establishes only absence from the public IEC catalogue at the cutoff. It does not establish that no unpublished committee draft exists, and it does not evaluate the technical merit of a draft-inspired method.

evidence_artifacts.label: request bodies, response hashes and bounded conclusion

records.claim_text: IFC's 2015 project-developer guide describes a DSRA as often equivalent to six months of debt service.
records.title: Utility-Scale Solar Photovoltaic Power Plants - A Project Developer's Guide
records.paraphrased_support: The guide describes six months as a common DSRA example and explains that the reserve covers debt shortfalls and is replenished if drawn.
records.limitations: This is generic 2015 solar-developer guidance, not IFC credit policy, not a 9-12-month requirement, and not a substitute for DutchBay financing documents.

records.claim_text: IFC's 2015 project-developer guide gives broad solar-project DSCR examples of at least 1.3x or 1.5x for merchant projects.
records.title: Utility-Scale Solar Photovoltaic Power Plants - A Project Developer's Guide
records.paraphrased_support: The guide lists broad typical terms for solar PV projects including DSCR of at least 1.3x or 1.5x for merchant projects.
records.limitations: The wording is illustrative guidance for solar PV; it does not prescribe one universal band for DSCR, LLCR, and PLCR or determine DutchBay covenant levels.

records.claim_text: An ADB-financed wind precedent maintained a six-month offshore DSRA while parent-guaranteed debt remained in place.
records.title: EDC Burgos Wind Power Corporation 150-Megawatt Burgos Wind Farm Project - Extended Annual Review Report
records.paraphrased_support: The review records an offshore DSRA covering scheduled principal and interest for the next six months and an EDC parent guarantee expected to remain until 2022.
records.limitations: This is one Philippines wind-refinancing precedent with transaction-specific support. It does not establish a universal ADB policy or DutchBay requirement.

records.claim_text: DSCR divides period CFADS by principal and interest debt service for that period.
records.publisher: Public Private Partnership Authority of Bangladesh with World Bank Group support
records.title: Public Private Partnership Handbook
records.paraphrased_support: The handbook defines DSCR at period t as CFADS for that period divided by principal and interest due for the period.
records.limitations: This high-level glossary does not define DutchBay's fee, tax, reserve, working-capital, or account-waterfall treatment and is not a lender term sheet.

records.claim_text: LLCR divides the NPV of future CFADS through loan maturity by debt outstanding at the measurement date.
records.publisher: Public Private Partnership Authority of Bangladesh with World Bank Group support
records.title: Public Private Partnership Handbook
records.paraphrased_support: The handbook defines LLCR as NPV of future CFADS from period t through the end of the loan divided by outstanding debt at period t.
records.limitations: The glossary does not select a discount curve or define DSRA, bridge, tranche, maturity, or timing treatment for DutchBay.

records.claim_text: PLCR uses future CFADS through project life rather than only loan life in the numerator.
records.publisher: Public Private Partnership Authority of Bangladesh with World Bank Group support
records.title: Public Private Partnership Handbook
records.paraphrased_support: The handbook defines PLCR as NPV of future CFADS from period t through project life divided by outstanding debt at period t.
records.limitations: PLCR is definitionally distinct from LLCR. The source supplies no universal covenant threshold and no DutchBay transaction term.

records.claim_text: The immutable P2 refuter files adjudicate 29 candidates: 25 live findings and four closed dispositions.
records.title: Finance Correctness Findings and six P2 refuter-verdict files
records.page_or_section: ranked table plus closed table; raw/P2_r1 through P2_r6
records.paraphrased_support: Direct enumeration gives 14 confirmed, 11 partially confirmed, one refuted, and three not-a-defect-by-design verdicts across 29 candidates; the 25-row ranked table is the live subset.
records.limitations: The audit's published 25-total and 12/10/1/2 breakdown conflates the live subset with the full population. The reconciliation preserves all six verdict-file hashes.

records.claim_text: Official IFC developer guidance identifies tariff, capex, energy yield, opex, interest and financing costs as lender-facing stress/sensitivity variables.
records.title: Utility-Scale Solar Photovoltaic Power Plants - A Project Developer's Guide
records.page_or_section: sections 15.4.2 and financial-modelling checklist; printed pages 178-181
records.paraphrased_support: The guide describes lender sensitivity analysis around key project variables, independent verification, stress/scenario analysis, and presentation of debt-service results.
records.limitations: This generic solar-developer guidance does not require every material risk to be a joint Monte Carlo dimension and does not specify DutchBay distributions or correlations.

records.claim_text: Official WBG-supported PPP guidance calls for comprehensive risk identification and allows qualitative and/or quantitative treatment, including Monte Carlo and sensitivity analysis.
records.publisher: Public Private Partnership Authority of Bangladesh with World Bank Group support
records.title: Public Private Partnership Handbook
records.paraphrased_support: The handbook identifies a broad project-risk universe, requires a risk matrix, and distinguishes qualitative assessment from quantitative tools such as Monte Carlo and sensitivity analysis.
records.limitations: It supports identification and appropriate treatment of material risks, not a universal rule that all risks must be sampled together or a DutchBay-specific stochastic design.

records.claim_text: The 2025 Sri Lanka PAD uses simultaneous Monte Carlo variation for selected economic uncertainties and separately records CEB/offtaker payment risk.
records.title: Secure, Affordable, and Sustainable Energy for Sri Lanka - Project Appraisal Document
records.paraphrased_support: The PAD reports Monte Carlo analysis of selected simultaneous uncertainties including capex overruns and construction delays, while separately rating sector/offtaker payment risk.
records.limitations: This programme economic analysis is precedent, not the DutchBay lender model, and does not prove that every separately identified risk belongs in one joint finance-MC distribution.

records.claim_text: Iman and Conover published a distribution-free rank-correlation method, but its full algorithm text was not obtained for this remediation cutoff.
records.publisher: Sandia National Laboratories / Communications in Statistics
records.title: A distribution-free approach to inducing rank correlation among input variables
records.page_or_section: OSTI abstract/metadata and Crossref bibliographic record; full text unavailable
records.paraphrased_support: Official metadata describes a distribution-free procedure that preserves marginals and induces a desired rank-correlation matrix.
records.limitations: The OSTI full-text endpoint returned HTTP 404 at the cutoff and no journal full text was archived. Metadata cannot verify the precise transform, correction matrix, or DutchBay implementation conformance.

records.claim_text: Latin hypercube sampling partitions each marginal range into equal-probability strata and permutes component assignments.
records.title: Comparison of Three Methods for Selecting Values of Input Variables in the Analysis of Output from a Computer Code
records.paraphrased_support: The primary paper defines the marginal stratification and permutation mechanics of Latin hypercube sampling.
records.limitations: This defines LHS mechanics; it does not validate DutchBay's approximate Gaussian-score rank-reordering as the corrected Iman-Conover algorithm.

records.claim_text: SciPy 1.17.1 implements LMS-plus-shift scrambled Sobol sampling; random_base2 uses powers of two, while independent scrambles are the basis for error estimation.
records.title: scipy.stats.qmc.Sobol source
records.paraphrased_support: The exact tagged source documents scrambling, the power-of-two balance guarantee, the non-power-of-two warning, and independent-scramble error-estimation use.
records.limitations: This verifies locked-library behavior only. It does not establish DutchBay convergence, replicated RQMC errors, SciPy-floor compatibility, or a research-SOTA differentiator.

records.claim_text: A non-degenerate Gaussian copula is asymptotically tail-independent under the classical coefficient.
records.title: Tail dependence of the Gaussian copula revisited
records.page_or_section: Corollary 1 and surrounding discussion; manuscript pages 8-9
records.paraphrased_support: The paper establishes zero classical Gaussian-copula tail-dependence for correlations below perfect dependence.
records.limitations: The mathematical property does not determine whether Gaussian dependence is acceptable for DutchBay; calibration, tail stress and transaction risk appetite remain owner judgments.

records.claim_text: SALib 1.5.2 implements Sobol sampling and A/B/AB/BA result analysis with defined sample structures.
records.title: SALib Sobol sampler and analyzer source
records.paraphrased_support: The exact tagged source defines the sampler and the D+2 or 2D+2 A/B/AB/BA output layout used by the analyzer.
records.limitations: Library conformance does not establish DutchBay sample sufficiency, convergence, rank stability, or freedom from bias when wrapper code deletes output-dependent rows.

records.claim_text: Saltelli describes efficient model-evaluation designs for computing variance-based sensitivity indices.
records.title: Making best use of model evaluations to compute sensitivity indices
records.paraphrased_support: The primary paper supplies the variance-based sensitivity-index sampling/estimation framework referenced by SALib.
records.limitations: It does not prescribe DutchBay sample sizes or validate wrapper handling of non-finite model outputs.

records.claim_text: Morris screening uses randomized one-factor-at-a-time elementary effects and summarizes their central tendency and spread.
records.title: Factorial Sampling Plans for Preliminary Computational Experiments
records.paraphrased_support: The primary paper defines the elementary-effects screening design and its interpretation.
records.limitations: It does not establish a universal DutchBay trajectory count or convergence threshold.

records.claim_text: Campolongo, Cariboni and Saltelli propose an enhanced Morris design and the absolute-mean elementary-effect statistic.
records.title: An effective screening design for sensitivity analysis of large models
records.paraphrased_support: The paper supplies the enhanced trajectory-selection and mu-star methodology used in modern Morris implementations.
records.limitations: The method paper does not prove the adequacy of DutchBay's chosen runs, seeds or acceptance thresholds.

records.claim_text: SALib 1.5.2 exposes Morris sampling and mu, mu-star and sigma analysis consistent with its cited method family.
records.title: SALib Morris sampler and analyzer source
records.paraphrased_support: The exact tagged source provides the implemented Morris sampling and result-statistic contract.
records.limitations: The library contract does not validate project-specific sample sufficiency or downstream row-deletion policy.

records.claim_text: Pianosi and Wagener introduced PAWN as a distribution-based sensitivity method comparing output CDFs.
records.publisher: University of Bristol / Environmental Modelling & Software
records.title: A simple and efficient method for global sensitivity analysis based on cumulative distribution functions
records.page_or_section: institutional publication record and abstract; journal pages 1-11
records.paraphrased_support: The institutional record and metadata identify the original PAWN CDF-based method and publication.
records.limitations: The 2015 full paper was not archived; method detail is therefore grounded in the archived 2018 primary follow-up and exact SALib source, not this metadata alone.

records.claim_text: PAWN can be estimated from a generic input-output sample using conditional and unconditional output CDF distances, with robustness checks and dummy factors.
records.title: Distribution-based sensitivity analysis from a generic input-output sample
records.paraphrased_support: The primary follow-up defines CDF/KS-based PAWN estimation, generic-sample use and robustness/dummy-factor diagnostics.
records.limitations: It does not prescribe a universal 0.15 noise floor or prove DutchBay sample convergence.

records.claim_text: SALib 1.5.2 computes PAWN indices from conditional/unconditional empirical CDF distances and reports distribution summaries.
records.title: SALib PAWN analyzer source
records.paraphrased_support: The exact tagged source defines the implemented PAWN CDF/KS calculations and returned statistics.
records.limitations: The source contains no universal project acceptance threshold; DutchBay's noise floor and sample adequacy remain unvalidated.

records.claim_text: For finite samples and scenario distributions, exact CVaR can differ from simple conditional tail means because probability mass at VaR may need fractional allocation.
records.title: Conditional Value-at-Risk for General Loss Distributions
records.paraphrased_support: The paper treats scenario/finite-sample discreteness and shows that exact CVaR splits probability mass at the VaR boundary to obtain the exact tail probability.
records.limitations: The paper defines the risk measure; DutchBay's numerical impact still requires controlled arrays and governed production-scale reproduction.

records.claim_text: IFC developer guidance defines P90 energy yield as production reached with 90 percent probability and says investors most often require P90 for financing.
records.title: Utility-Scale Solar Photovoltaic Power Plants - A Project Developer's Guide
records.page_or_section: section 2.6.1.2 and energy-yield discussion; printed pages 4 and 19
records.paraphrased_support: The guide frames P90 as an exceedance probability for energy production and as a commonly required financing case.
records.limitations: This energy-yield convention does not automatically determine adverse-direction labels for DSCR, IRR, costs, breach probabilities or every model KPI.

records.claim_text: Lee and Fields organize published wind losses/uncertainties against a proposed IEC 61400-15 framework and disclose categorization and correlation limitations.
records.publisher: Wind Energy Science / National Renewable Energy Laboratory
records.title: An overview of wind-energy-production prediction bias, losses, and uncertainties
records.paraphrased_support: The review uses a proposed IEC framework, records categories outside it, and cautions that public studies, classifications and uncertainty combinations are incomplete or assumption-dependent.
records.limitations: It is not a final IEC 61400-15-2 standard and does not prescribe DutchBay's six-of-seven taxonomy or a single-rho equicorrelation formula.

records.claim_text: MEASNET normally treats calculated AEP as P50 and derives P75/P90/P95 exceedance values from overall uncertainty, usually under a normal-distribution assumption.
records.title: Evaluation of Site-Specific Wind Conditions
records.paraphrased_support: MEASNET defines the wind-energy exceedance convention and states that uncertainties are usually assumed normal for deriving financing Pxx values.
records.limitations: The normal assumption is qualified as usual, not universally validated; it does not prove DutchBay's distribution choice or govern non-energy KPI directions.

records.claim_text: SciPy 1.17.1 bisection requires a sign-changing bracket and uses x-space absolute/relative tolerances rather than an absolute objective-value tolerance.
records.title: scipy.optimize.bisect source
records.paraphrased_support: The exact tagged source requires opposite endpoint signs and defines convergence with np.isclose in the root variable using xtol and rtol.
records.limitations: SciPy's contract does not itself prove DutchBay's scale-sensitive failure; that conclusion also requires the separate P2 numeric reproduction and repository code inspection.

limitations: The Iman-Conover journal/full algorithm text was not obtained; metadata is context_only and implementation conformance is not claimed.
The IEC 61400-15-2 evidence proves only absence from the official public catalogue at the cutoff, not absence of an unpublished committee draft.
Official guidance and precedents do not substitute for DutchBay facility, intercreditor, PPA, term-sheet, credit-approval or independent-engineer documents.
Library-source conformance does not establish project sample sufficiency, convergence, calibrated dependence, lender acceptance or research state of the art.
This controlled draft is an evidence register, not release approval or a regenerated Board/lender synthesis.
